evidence.quote: Table 4. The related parameters of HVS3
The first two types of HiVels are unbound stars, with speeds exceeding the escape velocity of the Milky Way (MW).

It is important to mention that the HVS3 (or HE 0437-5439) has a 40% probability of passing within 5 kpc of the LMC, taking into account the LMC’s influence (Edelmann et al. 2005; Erkal et al. 2019b).
We also calculated the trajectory of HVS3 (Erkal et al. 2019b) using the proper motion provided by Gaia DR3, and related parameters are listed in Table 4.

notes: Table 2 (T:p7-b1) explicitly gives the nine stars classed as unbound candidates; Gaia DR3 1309092223502856576, Gaia DR3 1204061267883975040, Gaia DR3 1297316350890352000, Gaia DR3 4263403134667526144, Gaia DR3 6098873935647575552, Gaia DR3 6241679678390298880, Gaia DR3 6235773131986833792, Gaia DR3 1383279090527227264, and Gaia DR3 1375165725506487424 are those nine entries, all with P_ub > 0.5. The text at T:p5-b4 says “8 for the first time, and 2 reported by Marchetti (2021) and Li et al. (2021)” for the nine stars; this conflicts with the nine-row Table 2 and its note identifying only the last two as previously reported, so the “8” count is treated as an apparent error. The last two entries are prior reports but are still current unbound candidates and are recorded as candidates_found because the present paper reports P_ub > 0.5. HVS3 (HE 0437-5439) is recorded as follow_up because T:p1-b7 defines HVSs as unbound, T:p2-b2 identifies HVS3, and T:p8-b4/Table 4 analyze it; no Gaia source ID is supplied, so no Gaia identifier is inferred.

Gaia DR3 1309092223502856576: Target is the first row of Table 2 (Gaia DR3 source_id 1309092223502856576), one of the 9 unbound candidates (P_ub > 0.5). The table reports P_disk = 0.002 and v_phi = 145 (+142/-112) km/s, which are not among the requested quantities. Galactocentric radius (r_GC), parallax, and proper motions are not reported for this star in the supplied paper (they are only available in the machine-readable catalog, Table 6, which is not provided). The paper reports only the unbound probability P_ub (0.729); no explicit bound probability is given.

Gaia DR3 1204061267883975040: The target is the second row of Table 2. The paper does not report parallax, proper-motion components, galactocentric radius, or bound probability for this star in the supplied material; P_disk and νφ are also listed but are not among the requested quantities.

Gaia DR3 4263403134667526144: The target Gaia DR3 4263403134667526144 is the fourth row of Table 2 (T:p7-b1; I:p7-b1) and is one of the 9 unbound candidates. The table does not report a bound probability, parallax, proper motions, or Galactocentric radius for this target, so those quantities are not extracted.

Gaia DR3 6098873935647575552: Gaia DR3 6098873935647575552 is the fifth row of Table 2 (the 9 unbound candidates). The paper does not report this star's parallax or proper motions individually (only HVS3 has tabulated proper motions in Table 4), so those quantities are omitted. The rotation velocity nu_phi = 345 (+200/-145) km/s given for this star is not one of the requested quantity identifiers.

Gaia DR3 6241679678390298880: The target Gaia DR3 6241679678390298880 is listed in Table 2 (T:p7-b1; I:p7-b1). Its reported P_ub = 0.549 marks it as an unbound candidate under the paper's P_ub > 0.5 criterion. The paper does not explicitly report a bound probability, so none was derived. No target-specific parallax, proper-motion components, or Galactocentric radius are given in the supplied tables.

Gaia DR3 6235773131986833792: The target, Gaia DR3 6235773131986833792, is listed in Table 2 among the 9 unbound candidates (the star is not one of the two previously reported in the last two rows). Table 2 does not report parallax or proper motions for this star, only the quantities extracted here. The paper's nu_GC is defined as the total velocity in the Galactocentric restframe and is recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. No bound probability, Galactocentric radius, or separate radial-velocity reference-frame distinction is reported for this star.

Gaia DR3 1383279090527227264: Target Gaia DR3 1383279090527227264 is row 8 of Table 2 (unbound candidates); the note states the last two rows list stars previously reported by Marchetti (2021); Li et al. (2021). The paper reports unbound probability Pub = 0.967 but does not report a separate bound probability, so none is given. No proper motions, parallax, or galactocentric radius are individually reported for this star in the supplied material.

Gaia DR3 1375165725506487424: The target (Gaia DR3 1375165725506487424) is the last row of Table 2, which lists the 9 unbound candidates (P_ub > 0.5). The table note states that the last two rows list stars already reported by Marchetti (2021) and Li et al. (2021); which of the two papers reported this specific star is not specified. P_disk = 1 and nu_phi = -319 +21 -26 km/s are also listed in Table 2 but are not among the requested quantities. No parallax, proper motions, or Galactocentric cylindrical/3D radius are reported for this star in the supplied material (those exist only in the machine-readable catalog described in Table 6, which is not provided).

HVS3: Target star: HVS3 / HE 0437-5439, whose parameters are given in Table 4 (T:p9-b1, I:p9-b1). Table 4's note states the first four rows (R.A., Decl., rv, d) are from Erkal et al. (2019b) and the last three rows (proper motions) are from Gaia DR3; this is reported here as the star's present-day state. Figure 5 / caption (T:p10-b0) gives velocities at closest approach to the LMC, described as Δv_HVS3−LMC = 790_{-63}^{+59} km/s; this is a velocity relative to the LMC, not a total speed in the Galactic rest frame, so it is not recorded as galactic_rest_frame_velocity. Likewise, the 37% (or 40% in the introduction, citing Edelmann et al. 2005; Erkal et al. 2019b) probability of passing within 5 kpc of the LMC is not a bound/unbound probability and is not recorded.
